title: Python Decision Making Quiz
description: Test your understanding of Python decision-making statements: if, if-else, and nested if.

questions.explanation: x=7 is greater than 5, so the if block executes and prints 'Greater'.
x=10 is divisible by 2, so the if block executes and prints 'Even'.

questions.question:
What does the following code print?

x = 5
y = 8
if x > 3 and y > 10:
    print('Yes')
else:
    print('No')
questions.explanation: x > 3 is True but y > 10 is False; the condition is not fully True, so else executes and prints 'No'.
x == 3 matches the elif condition, so it prints 'B'.
x > y is False, then nested if checks y % 2 == 0, which is True, so it prints 'Y is even'.
0 is considered False in Python, so the else block executes and prints 'False'.
x=9 satisfies x<10 in the elif block, so it prints 'Medium'.
x=3 and y=4, x>y is False, x==y is False, so else executes and prints 'Y is bigger'.
x >= 10 is True, then nested if x == 10 is True, so it prints 'Ten'.
x=7 does not satisfy x<5 or x>10, so else block executes and prints 'In'.
